items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to transportation service
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5861

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the tax law, in relation to transportation service


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To provide a technical correction to the tax law. Contrary to
legislative intent, NYC Livery transportation services were included
in a new transportation service tax provision created in the 09-10
budget. This legislation corrects that error by specifically excluding
from the sales tax those community car services defined as "Livery"
and "Base Station" by the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission
(TLC).

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Adds livery, as defined by section 6-01 of the rules and regulations
of the New York City taxi and limousine commission, to those
transportation services to be excluded under paragraph 34 of
subdivision (b) of section 1101 of the tax law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The NYC TLC defines Livery and Base Station as community car services
that serve as taxicabs for the outer boroughs and upper Manhattan.
Over the years, the NYC Livery industry has developed into an industry
that serves communities not serviced by yellow cabs. For these
underserved communities, the lack of yellow cabs is a significant
disadvantage that can prevent residents from attending simple
day-to-day activities.

The similarities between Manhattan "Yellow" cabs and the NYC
TLC-defined Livery cabs and Base Stations are numerous: from the need
for outside markings, the display of licenses, insurance and the
Passenger Bill of Rights, to the structure of fares, all of which
Black Cars and Luxury Limousines are not required to adhere to.

The state legislature never intended for NYC TLC defined Liveries and
Base Stations to be included in the new sales tax. Because of this
error, the community based car services in New York City were grouped
with a far more expansive definition of livery as provided by state
law. This legislation corrects the misapplication of the New York
State definition of livery.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
This bill represents no financial impact on the state due to the fact
that all revenue calculations had not included NYC Liveries

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to receipts
received on or after June 1, 2009.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to transportation service
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5861B

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the tax law, in relation to transportation service


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To provide a technical correction to the tax law. Contrary to
legislative intent, NYC Livery transportation services were included
in a new transportation service tax provision created in the 09-10
budget. This legislation corrects that error by specifically excluding
from the sales tax those community car services defined as "Livery"
and "Base Station" by the New York City Taxi and Limousine commission
(TLC). Additionally, this measure will exclude black car service from
the transportation service tax.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Adds livery and black car service, as defined by section 6-01 of the
rules and regulations of the New York city taxi and limousine
commission, to those transportation services to be excluded under
paragraph 34 of subdivision (b) of section 1101 of the tax law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The NYC TLC defines Livery and Base station as community car services
that serve as taxicabs for the outer boroughs and upper Manhattan.
over the years, the NYC Livery industry has developed into an industry
that serves communities not serviced by yellow cabs. For these under
served communities, the lack of yellow cabs is a significant
disadvantage that can prevent residents from attending simple
day-to-day activities.

The similarities between Manhattan "Yellow" cabs and the NYC
TLC-defined Livery cabs and Base stations are numerous: from the need
for outside markings, the display of licenses, insurance and the
Passenger Bill of Rights, to the structure of fares.

The state legislature never intended for NYC TLC defined Liveries and
Base Stations to be included in the new sales tax. Because of this
error, the community based car services in New York City were grouped
with a far more expansive definition of livery as provided by state
law.  This legislation corrects the misapplication of the New York
State definition of livery.

Black car service plays an integral role in a stressed transportation
system. The imposition of the transportation service tax places an
undue burden upon black car service and concurrently those who seek
their services.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
This bill represents no financial impact on the state due to the fact
that all revenue calculations had not included NYC Liveries. The
reduction of revenues experienced by black car service's exemption
from the transportation service tax is being determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to receipts
received on or after June 1, 2009.

summary: Excludes livery that is dispatched from a central facility.
